01_Citizens_Charter_2026.pdf.title: BIR Citizen's Charter 2026, 1st Edition
01_Citizens_Charter_2026.pdf.summary: Service standards for BIR external and internal services. Each external service lists the office or division, classification, who may avail, where to avail, operating hours, checklist of requirements, client steps, fees, and processing time. The charter also states the BIR mandate under Section 2 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, its mission, Aspiration 2028, and the PLEDGE service pledge. Use this document for walk-in and online RDO procedures, documentary requirements, fees, and processing time.

02_ORUS_User_Guide_2024.pdf.title: ORUS Taxpayer Guide: Application for TIN Issuance under Executive Order No. 98
02_ORUS_User_Guide_2024.pdf.reference: ORUS Application for TIN Issuance of E.O. 98 Taxpayer Guide
02_ORUS_User_Guide_2024.pdf.summary: Step-by-step ORUS guide for a Filipino citizen who does not yet have a TIN and needs one under Executive Order No. 98. It covers account creation, who must secure this TIN, account verification within 24 hours, and the BIR Form 1904 application through login. It is not a guide for business registration, books of accounts, or updating an existing business.
topics: TIN issuance without an existing TIN

sections.heading: Who must secure a TIN under E.O. 98
items: Dealings with banks
Dealings with government agencies
First-time job seeker
A person with no existing TIN or BIR record creates an ORUS account with one permanent or company email
A person who already has a TIN must use the permanent email already in the BIR registration record

sections.heading: Account creation
items: Open https://orus.bir.gov.ph from www.bir.gov.ph or directly
Choose New Registration, user type As an Individual, then Create an Account
Agree to the Terms of Service and register as Taxpayer
Choose Without Existing TIN and agree to the pop-up
User Type – Transaction: Get TIN for Filipino Citizen – E.O. 98 / One-Time Taxpayer
Taxpayer Type: Executive Order No. 98 – Filipino Citizen (EO98FC)
Required account fields include email, password, confirm password, and reCAPTCHA

Password must be 12 to 128 characters, must not match previous passwords or contain the username or full name, and must include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character
The email becomes the ORUS username, the permanent taxpayer email, and the address that receives the TIN after approval. Changing it is not available online

sections.heading: Account verification
items: After Register, verify the account from the email link within 24 hours
The verification link is on https://orus.bir.gov.ph
If the user did not start the transaction, do not click the link and report it to contact_us@bir.gov.ph
Concerns: telephone 8538-3200

sections.heading: Application for TIN issuance
items: Log in and choose New Registration, As an Individual, then Fill-up Registration Form (1904)
Complete Taxpayer Information and Residence Address
Purpose of TIN Application applies only to One-Time Transactions – Filipino Citizen (ONETFC); otherwise continue
Authorized Representative: No, or Yes with the required fields
Spouse Information is required only for married individuals
Upload attachments as JPEG, PNG, or PDF, each file not exceeding 25 MB
Review the summary, accept the caveats, and submit. The pop-up shows the Application Reference Number, date, and the Revenue District Office that will process it
Email is sent on submission and on approval. After approval, the TIN appears on the Profile tab with registered name, branch code, and RDO code
If denied, complete the findings in Reason or Comment for Denial and resubmit

03_Books_of_Accounts_ORUS_RMC_04_2026.pd.title: Clarification on Mandatory ORUS Registration of Permanently Bound Loose-Leaf and Computerized Books of Accounts (RMC No. 4-2026)
03_Books_of_Accounts_ORUS_RMC_04_2026.pd.summary: Clarifies that permanently bound loose-leaf books of accounts and computerized books of accounts must be registered through ORUS, and extends the deadlines because of ORUS log-in problems. This circular has no extractable text in the search index, so answer from this catalog entry.
topics: ORUS registration of books of accounts

sections.heading: Mandatory registration through ORUS
items: Issued to reiterate Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 3-2023

Permanently bound loose-leaf books of accounts and computerized books of accounts must be registered online through ORUS within the prescribed deadlines, unless the Commissioner or an authorized representative grants an extension requested before the original deadline lapses
Successful ORUS registration generates a QR code stamp that can be validated online
Affix the QR code to the first page of permanently bound loose-leaf books
Print the QR code and keep it for computerized books of accounts

sections.heading: Manual registration only in exceptional cases
items: Manual stamping at the RDO of the head office or branch where the TIN or branch TIN is registered is allowed only for system downtime or technical errors that prevent ORUS registration
Accept manual registration only with an official advisory that ORUS is unavailable, or a screenshot of the error message

sections.heading: Records not covered
items: Loose-leaf invoices, receipts, and other accounting records stay on manual registration at the concerned RDO because those transactions are not yet available in ORUS

sections.heading: Extended deadlines
items: Permanently bound loose-leaf books of accounts, invoices, and other accounting records: original deadline January 15, 2026, extended to January 31, 2026
Computerized books of accounts and other accounting records: original deadline January 30, 2026, extended to February 17, 2026
The extension is due to intermittent ORUS log-in connectivity issues
Taxpayers must comply within the extended deadlines to avoid penalties
Signed by Charlito Martin R. Mendoza, Commissioner of Internal Revenue

04_Invoicing_RMC_77_2024.pdf.title: Clarification on Invoicing Requirements under RR No. 7-2024, as amended by RR No. 11-2024 (RMC No. 77-2024)
04_Invoicing_RMC_77_2024.pdf.summary: Question-and-answer circular on the Ease of Paying Taxes Act invoicing rules. An invoice is the primary evidence for sales of goods and of services. Official receipts become supplementary documents. This circular has no extractable text in the search index, so answer from this catalog entry.

sections.heading: Who must issue an invoice
items: A VAT-registered person issues a VAT invoice for every sale, barter, exchange, or lease of goods or properties and for every sale, barter, or exchange of services, regardless of amount
A non-VAT person issues a non-VAT invoice for every sale of goods or properties and for every service valued at P500 or more. If the buyer asks for an invoice, issue it regardless of amount
A non-VAT seller also issues an invoice when a single transaction is more than P500, when the buyer requests one, or when transactions below P500 aggregate to at least P500 at the end of the day
The P500 threshold is adjusted every three years from January 22, 2024 using the Consumer Price Index
Invoicing provisions of RR No. 7-2024 took effect on April 27, 2024, fifteen days after publication on the BIR website on April 12, 2024

sections.heading: Invoice contents and names
items: A VAT or non-VAT invoice contains the information in Section 6(B) of RR No. 7-2024
Business style of the buyer or seller is not required. A trade name, store name, or branding may be shown
The word Invoice must be printed prominently. Allowed descriptive names include Invoice, Sales Invoice, Cash Invoice, Charge Invoice, Credit Invoice, Service Invoice, and Billing Invoice

Cash Invoice is for cash or immediately paid sales. Charge or Credit Invoice is for sales on credit. Service Invoice is for services. Billing Invoice bills charges for a specific transaction. Commercial Invoice is for export. Miscellaneous Invoice is for other income
From April 27, 2024, sellers of goods and services issue an invoice. A seller may use more than one type, such as cash and charge, or goods and services
A seller cannot issue a second invoice merely to acknowledge collection. A supplementary official receipt, payment receipt, or acknowledgement receipt may be issued when payment is collected
An invoice may itself show that payment was already received
Utility and other recurring billers issue a Billing Invoice when billing, with quantity, unit cost, and description or nature of service under Section 237 of the Tax Code

A VAT-registered seller with mixed transactions may use one invoice or separate invoices. One invoice must break down VATable, VAT-exempt, and zero-rated sales and the VAT for each. Separate invoices must prominently state VAT-Exempt Sale or Zero-Rated Sale

sections.heading: Authority to Print and official receipts
items: A new Authority to Print is required because the invoice is now the primary evidence. During the transitory period, unused official receipts may be converted
Unused official receipts may continue as supplementary documents only if every page is stamped THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT VALID FOR CLAIM OF INPUT TAX

Unused official receipts may be converted to invoices until fully consumed by striking out Official Receipt and stamping Invoice or a descriptive invoice name. Missing information required by Section 237, including quantity, unit cost, and description, may be stamped on conversion
Each invoice type may have its own serial range starting at 1, or a prefix or suffix. Official receipts kept as supplementary documents continue from the last approved official-receipt serial

CRM, POS, e-receipting, and e-invoicing systems may rename Official Receipt to a descriptive invoice term without RDO approval of the renaming. The new serial continues from the last official receipt. Submit a notice in duplicate to the RDO or Large Taxpayers office where the machines are registered, showing the starting serial and start date
Stamping Invoice on unused official receipts does not need prior RDO approval, but reporting the conversion is required. Obtain a new ATP before the converted receipts are used up
Inventory report of unused manual and loose-leaf official receipts converted to invoices, Annex C, was due until July 31, 2024
Notice of renaming for CRM, POS, CAS, or CBA, Annex D, was due within 30 days from completion of reconfiguration or on December 31, 2024, whichever came first
A taxpayer who already submitted the inventory under Annex D of RMO No. 12-2013, or a letter notice before this circular was posted, need not resubmit
Reports for all branches may be filed with the head-office RDO, which transmits copies to the branch RDOs, or through the TRRA Portal

CAS or CBA enhancements were to be done on or before December 31, 2024, with any extension approved by the Regional Director or the Assistant Commissioner of the Large Taxpayers Service for not more than six months from December 31, 2024. A letter request for extension was due before December 31, 2024. The RDO acts within three working days and the Regional Director or Assistant Commissioner acts within three working days of that recommendation

sections.heading: Consequences and special cases
items: Issuing an official receipt, stamped or unstamped, from CRM, POS, e-receipting, or e-invoicing after December 31, 2024 or completion of reconfiguration, whichever is first, and issuing an unstamped manual or loose-leaf official receipt after April 27, 2024, is treated as failure to issue an invoice under Section 6(A) of RR No. 7-2024
The penalty is not less than P1,000 and not more than P50,000, and imprisonment of not less than two years but not more than four years, under Section 264(a) of the Tax Code
Issuing only an official receipt, payment receipt, collection receipt, billing statement, or statement of account, without the corresponding invoice, has the same consequence

A non-VAT seller who issues a VAT invoice is liable for the VAT under Section 106 or 108 without the benefit of input tax credit, plus a 50 percent surcharge under Section 248(B). The VAT-registered buyer may claim input tax under Section 110 if the invoice shows the amount of sales, VAT amount, registered name and TIN from the COR of both parties, description of goods or services, and date

A VAT-registered seller who issues an invoice missing information required by Sections 3(B) and 6(B) of RR No. 7-2024 is liable for non-compliance. The buyer may still claim input tax unless the invoice lacks amount of sales, VAT amount, registered name and TIN, description, or date

For a sale of service before April 27, 2024 collected from January 22, 2024 through April 26, 2024, the collection document is an official receipt. If collected on or after April 27, 2024, the sale document is an invoice or a converted official receipt, and the collection document is a payment, collection, or acknowledgement receipt

For a sale of service on or after April 27, 2024, issue an invoice or an allowed converted official receipt. After April 27, 2024, collection is evidenced by a payment receipt, official receipt, collection receipt, or acknowledgement receipt

A non-stock, non-profit educational, charitable, religious, cultural, social welfare, or philanthropic entity, or an NGO, issues a supplementary document such as a non-VAT official receipt, acknowledgement receipt, or donation receipt for donations. If it has any profitable business activity, it issues an invoice for every business sale of goods or services
Sample manual invoice layouts are attached as annexes. Signed by Romeo D. Lumagui, Jr., Commissioner of Internal Revenue. Effectivity is upon posting on the BIR website

05_Online_Sellers_Taxpayer_Guide.pdf.title: Taxpayer's Guide for Online Sellers: Steps and Requirements for Registration, Filing, and Payment
05_Online_Sellers_Taxpayer_Guide.pdf.issued: Prepared by the Public Information and Education Division under the Client Support Service
05_Online_Sellers_Taxpayer_Guide.pdf.summary: Guide for online sellers earning income in the Philippines through an electronic platform or their own website, except non-resident foreign companies. It covers five registration channels, post-registration duties, income tax rates, filing deadlines, withholding reports, and BIR eServices.

sections.heading: Ways to register
items: Manual registration at the New Business Registration Counter of the RDO of the place of business, or of the residence if the business is at home, under the Single Window Policy
ORUS at https://orus.bir.gov.ph for end-to-end registration and updates
NewBizReg Portal at https://www.bir.gov.ph/newbizreg/ for a new head office or branch, with scanned documents emailed to the RDO and attachments not exceeding 4 MB per email
TRRA Portal at https://www.bir.gov.ph/trraportal/ for other registration transactions, each PDF not exceeding 4 MB
Philippine Business Hub at https://business.gov.ph/home, which connects SEC, DTI, BIR, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and selected Metro Manila LGUs
Register on or before commencement of business, payment of any tax due, or filing of a return, whichever comes first

sections.heading: Manual registration documents and fees
items: Individuals: BIR Form 1901, a government-issued ID showing name, address, and birth date, or other proof of address, and either a final sample of own invoices with BIR Form 1906 or BIR Printed Invoices bought at the NBRC
Additional for individuals if applicable: DTI certificate for a business name, and an SPA plus IDs if a representative transacts

Corporations: BIR Form 1903, SEC Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Recording for a partnership, or License to Do Business for a foreign corporation, Articles of Incorporation, and invoice sample with BIR Form 1906 or BIR Printed Invoices
Additional for corporations transacting through a representative: board resolution or secretary's certificate, and government IDs
Pay P30 Documentary Stamp Tax and, if chosen, the cost of BIR Printed Invoices. An Authority to Print is filed at the NBRC when printing own invoices
Receive the Certificate of Registration, received copy of BIR Form 1901 or 1903, Notice to Issue Invoice, BIR Printed Invoices or Authority to Print, and proof of payment
Newly registered taxpayers are encouraged to attend the RDO taxpayer briefing. Other documents are in the Citizen's Charter

sections.heading: ORUS, NewBizReg, TRRA, and Philippine Business Hub
items: ORUS: create an account, choose new registration, accomplish BIR Form 1901 or 1903, attach the same ID, invoice, SEC, and SPA documents, pay the P30 loose DST online through Link.BizPortal using LANDBANK, BPI, Asia United Bank, PSBank, RCBC, Robinsons Bank, or UnionBank, then print the electronic COR and ATP if applicable

NewBizReg: an applicant with a TIN may pay the P30 DST online. An applicant without a TIN waits for an email and pays the DST at the NBRC when claiming the COR. Attach the tax type questionnaire from the NewBizReg site

TRRA transactions: TIN under E.O. 98 and ONETT, registration of OFW and non-resident citizens, Authority to Print, email update using Form S1905, transfer of employees and other non-business taxpayers, and updating a maiden name for a married woman

Philippine Business Hub: create a profile, register the business name in BNRS, answer the BIR tax type questionnaire, pay P30 DST online or manually, generate or claim the COR, then apply for an ATP or buy BIR Printed Invoices. Manual payment needs the PBH Unified Application Form, tax type questionnaire, and invoice sample or BIR Printed Invoices

sections.heading: After registration
items: Post the Certificate of Registration and Notice to Issue Invoices where they are visible in the establishment

Register books of accounts before the deadline of the first quarterly income tax return or the annual income tax return, whichever is earlier. New sets may be registered yearly before the old pages are used up
Annual sales, earnings, and receipts exceeding P3,000,000 must be audited yearly by an independent CPA
Preserve books and other accounting records for five years from the day after the filing deadline, or from the actual filing date if filed late, counted from the taxable year of the last entry

Issue a registered sales or commercial invoice for every sale or transfer of merchandise or service of P500 or more. If each sale is below P500 but the day's total is at least P500, issue one invoice for the day's aggregate. VAT-registered persons issue an invoice regardless of amount

sections.heading: Tax rates
items: Domestic corporation and resident foreign corporation: 25 percent of taxable income, or 20 percent if net taxable income does not exceed P5,000,000 and total assets excluding the land of the office, plant, and equipment do not exceed P100,000,000
Minimum corporate income tax: 2 percent of gross income, or 1 percent from July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2023, reverting to 2 percent on July 1, 2023
Non-resident foreign corporation: 25 percent of taxable income from Philippine sources

Graduated individual income tax: 0 up to P250,000; 15 percent of the excess over P250,000 up to P400,000; P22,500 plus 20 percent of the excess over P400,000 up to P800,000; P102,500 plus 25 percent of the excess over P800,000 up to P2,000,000; P402,500 plus 30 percent of the excess over P2,000,000 up to P8,000,000; P2,202,500 plus 35 percent of the excess over P8,000,000

The 8 percent income tax option is for self-employed individuals whose gross sales and other non-operating income do not exceed the P3,000,000 VAT threshold, and for mixed-income earners on their business income only. Compensation income stays on graduated rates. Exceeding the threshold ends the option

First year: signify the 8 percent option on BIR Form 1901 or on the initial quarterly return, BIR Form 2551Q or 1701Q. Later years: BIR Form 1905 at the start of the year, or the first quarterly percentage tax or income tax return

sections.heading: Filing deadlines for self-employed individuals
items: Income tax BIR Form 1701Q: May 15, August 15, and November 15. Annual BIR Form 1701 or 1701A: April 15
VAT BIR Form 2550Q: April 25, July 25, October 25, and January 25 of the following year
Percentage tax BIR Form 2551Q: the same quarterly dates as VAT

VAT applies when gross sales exceed P3,000,000 or the person opts to register as a VAT taxpayer. Percentage tax applies to a VAT-covered activity whose gross sales do not exceed P3,000,000 and who is not VAT-registered

sections.heading: Filing deadlines for corporations, partnerships, and other non-individuals
items: Quarterly income tax BIR Form 1702Q: within 60 days after the close of each taxable quarter, calendar or fiscal
Annual income tax BIR Form 1702-RT, 1702-EX, or 1702-MX: the 15th day of the fourth month after the close of the taxable year
VAT BIR Form 2550Q and percentage tax BIR Form 2551Q: the 25th day after the close of each taxable quarter

sections.heading: How to file and what else to submit
items: Manual filing of hard copies at an authorized agent bank or revenue collection officer
eBIRForms offline package
eFPS for electronic filing and online payment
eAFS for online submission of the filed income tax return, audited financial statements, and other attachments in PDF

Under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act, Republic Act No. 11976, returns are filed electronically and tax may be paid electronically or manually at any authorized agent bank, RDO through a revenue collection officer, payment gateway, or authorized tax software provider
ePayment channels are listed at the BIR ePay page
BIR Form 0619-E and 0619-F: on or before the 10th day of the following month for the first two months of the quarter. eFPS users follow RR No. 26-2002
BIR Form 1601-C: on or before the 10th day of the following month for January to November, and on or before January 15 for December
BIR Forms 1601-EQ, 1601-FQ, and 1603Q: not later than the last day of the month after the quarter
SAWT through eSubmission when claiming creditable withholding tax on BIR Forms 1701, 1701A, 1701Q, 2550Q, and 2551Q
SLSP through eSubmission as an attachment to BIR Form 2550Q under RMO No. 4-2003
QAP as an attachment to BIR Form 1601-EQ
BIR Form 1604-E and the annual alphalist of payees: on or before March 1 of the following year
BIR Forms 1604-C and 1604-F: on or before January 31 of the following year

06_eBIRForms_Job_Aid.pdf.title: Job Aids for Taxpayers and Accredited Tax Agents for the Use of the eBIRForms
06_eBIRForms_Job_Aid.pdf.summary: January 2013 job aid for the offline eBIRForms package and the online eBIRForms system. It explains the project, installation, offline preparation, printing and signing, online enrollment, and online filing. Procedures and screen labels are those of this edition, not a later package.

sections.heading: Project overview
items: The interactive-forms project supports electronic filing, wider channels than eFPS, data capture, and filing by people with limited internet
Phase 1: downloadable PDF of BIR Forms 1700, 1701, and 1702 that can be filled, saved, printed, and submitted manually
Phase 2: offline package of 31 BIR forms with entry, editing, saving, and printing, still submitted manually

Phase 3: online system that accepts, validates, processes, and stores returns and sends data to ITS and RPS. It serves non-eFPS taxpayers, accredited tax agents filing for clients, and tax software providers certifying their software

sections.heading: Terms and features
items: Offline means not connected to the internet. Online means connected
Manual filing: fill offline, print, and submit to an authorized agent bank, RDO, or revenue collection officer
Electronic filing in this job aid: fill the offline package or the downloadable Excel or PDF forms 1700, 1701, and 1702
Manual payment is handed to an authorized agent bank or revenue collection officer. Electronic payment uses an enrolled payment system
The offline package validates required fields, single options, MMDDYYYY dates, allowed values, and data length, and it computes fields automatically
The forms in the package are the existing BIR forms in electronic format, not new forms

sections.heading: How the job aid is organized
items: Introduction to eBIRForms
Download and install the offline package
Update the offline version
Navigate a form and the types of input

07_COR_eCOR_Registration_Seal_RMC_38_202.title: Issuance and Posting of the BIR Registration Seal Badge and QR Code on the Certificate of Registration (RMC No. 38-2026)
07_COR_eCOR_Registration_Seal_RMC_38_202.summary: Requires online sellers and persons offering services online to post the BIR Registration Seal Badge instead of the full COR or eCOR, and announces the QR code on the COR and eCOR. This circular has no extractable text in the search index, so answer from this catalog entry.

sections.heading: Legal basis and who is covered
items: Based on Section 236 of the Tax Code, Section 5 of RR No. 7-2024, and Section 5 of RR No. 15-2024

Persons subject to internal revenue tax must register with the RDO on or before commencement of business, before payment of any tax due, or before or upon filing a return, whichever the Tax Code requires
Section 5(F) of RR No. 7-2024 requires issuance of a COR or eCOR for each head office, branch, and facility after complete documentary requirements, within the Citizen's Charter period
Persons engaged in business or practice of profession must post the COR or eCOR where the business is conducted and at each branch or facility, clearly visible to the public
Section 5(H) of RR No. 7-2024 and Section 7 of RR No. 15-2024 require proof of registration on websites, e-commerce or e-marketplace seller pages, and other platforms

Coverage includes online sellers of goods and persons providing services digitally, including professionals, bloggers, vloggers, live streamers, content creators, influencers, and individuals earning from views, advertisements, affiliate commissions, brand sponsorships, or similar monetized digital activities

sections.heading: Registration Seal Badge
items: The BIR issues the badge in Annex A so the seller, content creator, or influencer can post it instead of the full COR or eCOR
It is issued with the COR or eCOR, free of charge, manually or electronically through ORUS, to all business taxpayers
Online sellers and online service providers must have the applicable PSIC or PSOC on the COR or eCOR
Individual professional: PSOC 5990, Online Content Creator
Individual and non-individual: PSIC 47913 retail sale via internet; PSIC 47911 retail sale via mail order; PSIC 47912 retail sale via telephone order; PSIC 85593 online tutorial services

Both the COR or eCOR and the badge contain a QR code. Scan it with a mobile application or QR scanner. Relying parties must confirm that the URL is the official BIR verification domain or the BIR link https://verify.bir.gov.ph/correspondence/ before relying on the result

An existing COR or eCOR without a QR code does not have to be replaced, but taxpayers are encouraged to update it. Someone required to post proof online secures the badge by updating registration at the RDO or through ORUS and paying the P30 loose Documentary Stamp Tax

sections.heading: Where and how to post it
items: Taxpayer's own website or mobile application: any page or link such as About, Company, Government Compliance, or Business Permits
E-commerce platform or mobile app: Support, About, App Setting, or a link such as Government Compliance or Business Permits
Seller, merchant, or service provider with an account or sales on a platform: the seller or merchant page, profile, store or shop details, marketplace, or business page
Post only the badge, not the entire registration document. Cropping or extracting the badge is allowed. Annex B shows the display
The uploaded badge must stay clear, readable, and unaltered
The COR or eCOR with QR code and the badge become available when the circular is published on www.bir.gov.ph. Annex C is the taxpayer guide for generating and securing the badge through ORUS
Signed by Charlito Martin R. Mendoza, Commissioner of Internal Revenue

08_Taxpayer_Portal_RMC_53_2026.pdf.title: Availability and Pilot Implementation of the Taxpayer Portal (RMC No. 53-2026)
08_Taxpayer_Portal_RMC_53_2026.pdf.summary: Announces the Taxpayer Portal and limits the pilot to taxpayers registered under the Large Taxpayers Service. It is a secured single view of registration, filed returns, payments, the account ledger, and filing or payment reminders.

sections.heading: Pilot coverage and functions
items: Pilot is only for taxpayers registered under the offices or divisions of the Large Taxpayers Service
View current registration details
Monitor the status of filed returns by tax type and form type
Track tax payments
View the account ledger by tax type and form type
Receive system-generated notifications and reminders for filing and payment
The portal is meant to reduce manual follow-up and in-person visits

sections.heading: Where to get help
items: For enrollment, technical concerns, or inaccurate records, coordinate with the Large Taxpayers office or division where the taxpayer is registered

09_Books_of_Accounts_CDR_2024.pdf.title: BIR Checklist of Documentary Requirements, Revised January 2024
09_Books_of_Accounts_CDR_2024.pdf.summary: Cover-sheet checklists for registration and registration-related applications. Processing starts only when documents are complete; incomplete applications are returned. Mark submitted documents and mark lacking ones. The file includes books of accounts as one checklist, F1105B, together with the other registration checklists.

sections.heading: F1101 — Self-employed individuals
items: Covers sole proprietors, PRC-regulated professionals, and persons not regulated by the PRC such as artists, directors, freelancers, mixed-income earners, job order or service contractors, online sellers, vloggers, bloggers, streamers, influencers, YouTubers, and content creators
Online: create an ORUS account at https://orus.bir.gov.ph. After paying P30 loose DST, print the electronic COR. Comply with invoicing through BIR Printed Invoices or an Authority to Print

Manual: BIR Form 1901, two originals; government-issued ID showing name, address, and birth date, or proof of address. PRC professionals submit a valid PRC ID plus an ID or proof of address. Online applications upload a selfie while holding the ID
Buy BIR Printed Invoices at the New Business Registrant Counter, or submit one original final sample of own invoices and use an accredited printer
Fee: P30 loose Documentary Stamp Tax on the COR, plus the printing cost of BIR Printed Invoices if chosen. If the DST was paid online, submit a photocopy of the proof

If applicable: SPA and IDs for a representative, DTI certificate for a business name, 9(g) work visa for a foreign national, service contract for a job order or service contract with an NGA, LGU, GOCC, or GFI, franchise documents for a common carrier, BMBE Certificate of Authority, and proof of registration with BOI, PEZA, BCDA, TIEZA, SBMA, or a similar zone

sections.heading: F11ET — Estate and trust
items: BIR Form 1901, two originals

Estate with property subject to estate tax or under judicial settlement: photocopy of the decedent's death certificate. The heir, administrator, or executor requests cancellation of the decedent's TIN
Irrevocable trust: photocopy of the irrevocable trust agreement
No fee listed
Representative of a trust: SPA from the trustee or trustor and government IDs. Administrator, executor, or heir: proof of that capacity and a government ID

sections.heading: F1103 — Corporations, partnerships, cooperatives, and associations
items: Covers a domestic corporation, one-person corporation, partnership, resident foreign corporation, cooperative, and association, whether taxable or non-taxable
Online through ORUS, with electronic COR after P30 loose DST and invoicing compliance
Manual: BIR Form 1903, two originals

One photocopy of the SEC Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of recording for a partnership, license to do business for a foreign corporation, CDA certificate, HLURB certificate, or DOLE certificate, as applicable
One photocopy of the articles of incorporation, partnership, or cooperation, articles of association, or the constitution and by-laws of a labor organization
BIR Printed Invoices or one original final sample of own invoices

sections.heading: F11PBH — Registration through the Philippine Business Hub
items: Covers self-employed persons, domestic corporations, one-person corporations, partnerships, and foreign corporations

Manual COR: two originals of the printed PBH Unified Form, one original accomplished tax type questionnaire, and either BIR Printed Invoices or BIR Form 1906 with a final invoice sample from an accredited printer
DST: two originals of BIR Form 0605 for the P30 loose stamp, plus BIR Printed Invoice cost if chosen
A taxpayer who already generated the electronic COR after online payment of P30 DST still complies with invoicing through BIR Printed Invoices or an Authority to Print
A representative needs an SPA for an individual, or a board resolution, written resolution, or secretary's certificate for a non-individual, plus IDs

sections.heading: F11BF — Branch and facility
items: Online: the head office enrolls in ORUS at https://orus.bir.gov.ph and registers the branch or facility. Electronic COR follows payment of P30 loose DST. A branch, but not a facility, must comply with invoicing
Manual branch: BIR Form 1901 or 1903, two originals, plus BIR Printed Invoices or a final sample of own invoices
Manual facility: BIR Form 1901 or 1903, two originals
Fee: P30 loose DST on the COR. BIR Printed Invoice cost applies to a branch only
A representative needs an SPA or a board or secretary's certificate, plus IDs

sections.heading: F1102 — Employees, registered through the employer
items: The employer creates an ORUS account and enrolls in Employer Service Link at https://orus.bir.gov.ph
Local employee already hired: BIR Form 1902, two originals, and a government-issued ID. Online filing uploads a selfie while holding the ID
Foreign national employee: BIR Form 1902 and a photocopy of the passport bio page, including entry or exit stamps if applicable
IGL or POGO employees also submit a certified true copy of the employment contract or equivalent showing duration, compensation, benefits, and duties
No fee

If applicable: marriage contract for a married woman. If the employer secures the TIN manually because the system is unavailable, a letter of authority on company letterhead signed by the president or HR head

sections.heading: F1104 — Purely TIN issuance
items: E.O. 98 and ONETT, local individual or resident alien: BIR Form 1904, two originals, and a government-issued ID. Transfer of property by succession also needs the death certificate or an extrajudicial settlement or affidavit of self-adjudication
If applicable: marriage contract for a married woman, SPA and IDs for a representative, and a barangay certification for a first-time job seeker
E.O. 98, nonresident foreign national: BIR Form 1904 and the passport bio page. A representative needs an apostilled SPA

sections.heading: F1106 — Authority to Print invoices
items: New or subsequent ATP for manual bound invoices: BIR Form 1906, two originals; choose an accredited printer; one original final sample of own invoices or supplementary invoices
Subsequent bound application also needs the last ATP, the printer's certificate of delivery, or presentation of a booklet from the last ATP
Manual loose-leaf invoices: BIR Form 1906, a photocopy of the Permit to Use loose-leaf invoices, a final sample, and the last ATP for a subsequent application
No fee listed on this checklist
A representative needs an SPA or a board resolution, written resolution, or secretary's certificate, plus IDs

sections.heading: F1105B — Registration of books of accounts
items: Online through ORUS at https://orus.bir.gov.ph. Successful registration generates a QR stamp to paste on the first page of the books
New or subsequent manual books: BIR Form 1905, two originals, and the new set of permanently bound books

Manual loose-leaf books: BIR Form 1905, photocopy of the Permit to Use, the permanently bound loose-leaf books, and an original affidavit of completeness, accuracy, and the number of loose leaves used

Computerized books: BIR Form 1905, photocopy of the acknowledgement certificate or Permit to Use for the CAS or CBA if applicable, a transmittal letter, and a labeled DVD, USB, or other storage holding the electronic books in the Standard Audit File, plus an original affidavit of completeness and appropriateness

sections.heading: F1100 — Permit to Use loose-leaf books of accounts or invoices
items: Online through ORUS. The permit may be downloaded and printed
BIR Form 1900, two originals
One original sample format and print-out

One original sworn statement identifying the books, invoices, receipts, and other records, the serial numbers of principal and supplementary invoices or receipts, and a commitment to bind the loose-leaf forms permanently within 15 days after the end of each taxable year or when their use ends
No fee
A representative needs an SPA or a board or secretary's certificate, plus IDs

sections.heading: F1105 — Registration information updates and TIN card
items: These updates are free online in ORUS: Digital TIN ID, contact information, contact person, civil status, residence address, transfer of registration record, additional line of business, new business name, new tax types or form types, and the 8 percent income tax option

Paper TIN card: BIR Form 1905, one original; latest 1x1 photo; government-issued ID. Personal appearance is mandatory. The first paper card is free. Replacement of a lost or damaged card costs P100, and a lost card needs an affidavit of loss. A fake TIN card is confiscated for destruction

Change of registered business address within the same RDO: BIR Form 1905, two originals, and a photocopy of the mayor's permit, DTI certificate, SEC certificate, or the appointment-of-officers form for a one-person corporation showing the new address

sections.heading: F1105T — Transfer of registration
items: Individuals not engaged in business, meaning E.O. 98, ONETT, or employee: BIR Form 1905, two originals

Business transfer to another RDO, head office or branch: submit three originals of BIR Form 1905 to the old RDO, all stamped Received. One copy goes to the new RDO with the Transfer Related Docket, one stays with the old RDO, and one stays with the taxpayer

Also submit to the old RDO three originals of the inventory of unused invoices, for destruction or for approval to use them in the new RDO, and three originals of a notarized Transfer Commitment Form if there are open cases
Submit to the new RDO two originals of BIR Form 1905. Non-individuals also submit the amended articles showing the new principal address and the certificate of filing of the amended articles

sections.heading: F1105C — Cancellation of TIN or closure
items: Death or identical or multiple TINs: BIR Form 1905, two originals, and a photocopy of the death certificate in case of death

Closure of a head office or branch, or cancellation because of dissolution, merger, or consolidation: BIR Form 1905; original list of ending inventory of goods, supplies, and capital goods; inventory and the unused invoices, supplementary invoices, and other unused accounting forms; original business notices and permits such as the ATP, NIRI, and CRM or POS accreditation and permit; and the original Certificate of Registration
No fee
A representative needs an SPA or a board resolution, written resolution, or secretary's certificate, plus IDs
